page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the e2 family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.2 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is configured with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of memory per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates a mixed performance profile. The instance achieves strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and PassMark CPU metrics fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached read/write operations is average, as is the static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, perform poorly, falling into the bottom 10% to 25% of tested systems.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the e2-highcpu-16 offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints. It is suitable for tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and basic web serving. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases or heavy text-processing pipelines due to its constrained memory capacity and lower single-threaded decompression speeds.
